literal: Pleasure to a person begging, those things begged, pain without causing, if they come.
translation: Even begging becomes a pleasure to a person if the things they ask for are given without causing any pain or distress.
modern: ஒருவருக்குப் பிறரிடம் இரந்து கேட்பது இன்பமாகும், அவ்வாறு இரந்து கேட்ட பொருள்கள் துன்பம் தராமல் கிடைக்குமானால்.
explanation: This couplet explains that the act of begging, which is usually painful and humiliating, can actually bring joy under a specific condition. That condition is when the requested items (இரந்தவை) are given freely and gracefully, without causing any distress (துன்பம் உறாஅ) or humiliation to the seeker. The key phrase 'துன்பம் உறாஅ வரின்' highlights that the manner of giving determines the emotional outcome of the request. When met with immediate and painless generosity, the act of asking becomes a source of happiness rather than shame.
